failure_summary: Runs 0-1 are clean, but three of five runs fail on the annotation/handle layer with everything needed present in the assembled prompt: run 2 writes the raw square 'c5r6' into player-facing prose (OI-194) though the prompt explicitly says 'Never write a raw square' (the render's own L2 link.text supplies 'c5r6', so the render seeds it); run 3 emits [zone:opp-major-2] as a bare noun, triggering annotationRepairs ['unclosed_tag:zone:played-col'] (G7 auto-fail) which rebinds the c5r6 highlight to 'rather than play your chosen column' and leaves the stripped prose reading 'You needed to take the block at  rather than play your chosen column' with column 1 never named (A6 fail); run 4 emits NO tags at all, dropping both required handles (opp-major-2, opp-key-line) so 'the key top-row square' and 'the line along the top-right' point at nothing (A7b) - that omission is partly an OI-183 eval artifact since production would have retried on the missing required set. This is a production-fidelity run on gpt-5.4-mini, so prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability. Model-independent secondary: assembleGroundedPrompt renders lostResource.line as four EMPTY objects ([{},{},{},{}]) - ply/mover/col/cell are suppressed even though render_decision.fieldPartition.rendered lists lostResource.line[].ply/.mover/.col/.cell - so the forced denial sequence (you take c1r6, then c5r6) that is the real reason column 1 holds the draw was never shown to the model, and no run explains it.
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 are null (not scored) on those axes. A1/A2/A6 copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_subset_2026-08-26T15-47-56Z_mechanical.json (A6 fail on run 3 only). Board verified with ./visualize_board.sh 3333311115554535522024412246261666006: only cols 1 and 5 are playable; P1(X) holds major threats at col1 row6 and col5 row6; solver scr row gives col1=0 (draw) and col5=-2 (loss), confirming bestCol 0 / playedCol 4 and case draw_to_lose. A3/A4 runs 0-1: after the played col5 disc lands at c5r5 the opponent's c5r6 becomes gravity-top and completes c4r6.c5r6.c6r6.c7r6 (row 6 = O,_,O,O on cols 4-7), so 'you handed them the top-edge square and let their next move finish the threat' is board-true and decisive; cells checked against render_decision.finalMovestring 33333111155545355220244122462616660064, not an alternate PV. A5 run 2: raw cNrM 'c5r6' in the mechanism prose - known OI-194. A5 run 3 passes the enumerated A5a tests (2nd person, no field names) but the served prose is incoherent after markup stripping because of the repair; recorded under G7/A7b rather than double-charged. A5b not applicable (player 2 but boardState is 'closing', not 'opening'). A7c N/A on every run - the mechanism named is an immediate threat, not a fork; note that no *-fork-pivot handle exists in render_decision.zones.aliases anyway. G3 pass: afterBest is shown:false and no run needed it. G5 pass runs 0-1: the decision-board tactic list (major c1r6, major c5r6, double c1r6/c5r6) and the afterPlayed list (immediate c5r6) are both board-true per visualize_board. Additional render finding not charged to any axis: the offered alias opp-double has spec 'windows:c1r6,c5r6' but role text 'the single fork square where your opponent gets two winning squares at once' - the role says one square while the spec is two, a shape mismatch that would mis-highlight if used (no run used it).

counterexamples.evidence: Run 2 prose: 'let your opponent take the key square at c5r6' - raw cNrM notation reaches the player, while the same prompt's Highlightable-regions block says 'Never write a raw square'; the L2 link text itself reads 'Your move let the opponent occupy c5r6, ...', supplying the notation the model echoed.

Run 3 raw emits '[zone:opp-major-2] rather than play [zone:played-col]your chosen column[/zone:played-col]' - the bare opening tag used as a noun is exactly the 'Bad' pattern the prompt warns against; repair 'unclosed_tag:zone:played-col' rebinds the c5r6 highlight to 'rather than play your chosen column' and swallows the played-col highlight.

Run 4 emits zero [zone:] tags despite both handles being in requiredSet, so 'the key top-row square', 'the four-in-a-row line along the top-right' and 'the top-right stretch' resolve to nothing on screen; production retries on a missing required handle, so the single-call harness overstates this.

assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv)) renders "line": [{},{},{},{}] - the prompt contains no 'ply' key and never mentions c1r5 or c1r6 as part of a sequence, so the forced denial line (ply39 X c1r5, ply40 you c1r6, ply41 X c5r5, ply42 you c5r6) that explains WHY column 1 holds the draw is absent from what the model saw, even though render_decision.fieldPartition.rendered claims those paths are rendered.
